words.sense: Firmly refuse to accept a claim, accusation, idea, or association.
misconceptions: A strong denial automatically proves a claim wrong.

words.sense: Demonstrate that a claim is wrong through evidence or reasoning.
misconceptions: Proof and refusal are interchangeable acts.

semantic_axes.description: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.

edges.boundary_rule: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.

misconceptions.M1: A strong denial automatically proves a claim wrong.
misconceptions.M2: Proof and refusal are interchangeable acts.
misconceptions.M3: Being publicly opposed to an idea is evidence against its truth.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Amina’s response to the rumor?

beats.text: Amina said, “I will not accept that accusation, and I want my name removed from it.”
beats.reason: She makes her rejection unmistakable without disproving it.

beats.text: She repeated the same statement when asked in front of the whole class.
beats.reason: A larger audience does not turn the statement into a demonstration.

chains.feedback_short: Amina rejects the accusation firmly; repeating it publicly supplies no proof.
chains.feedback_deep: To repudiate is to reject something emphatically. To refute it requires evidence or reasoning that shows the accusation is false.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.attention: Ask whether she simply denies it or demonstrates its error.
hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Jorge’s reply to the complaint?

beats.text: Jorge answered, “I do not accept your claim that I collected the missing parcel at noon.”
beats.reason: The response is a denial without evidence.

beats.text: He attached the signed delivery receipt showing the named customer collected that parcel at noon, not Jorge.
beats.decisive_clue: signed receipt disproves the alleged noon collection
beats.reason: The supporting record demonstrates that Jorge did not collect the parcel at noon.

chains.feedback_short: Jorge first rejects the allegation; the signed receipt then demonstrates that he did not collect the parcel at noon.
chains.feedback_deep: Repudiation means refusing an allegation. Refutation goes further: evidence shows why the specific allegation is untrue. The receipt provides that decisive support.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.attention: What does the attached record establish?
hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Sora’s response to the proposed answer?

beats.text: Sora checked the total and showed that adding 14, 18, and 12 gives 44, not 54.
beats.decisive_clue: arithmetic directly contradicts the stated total
beats.reason: The calculation demonstrates the answer is wrong.

beats.text: She wrote the addition vertically so every classmate could check each column.
beats.reason: Making the proof easy to inspect strengthens it.

chains.feedback_short: A checkable addition demonstrates the error; it does more than express disagreement.
chains.feedback_deep: To refute is to establish falsity by sound reasons or evidence. Showing the calculation is exactly such a demonstration.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Ben’s statement about an advertisement?

beats.text: Ben announced that he wanted nothing to do with the advertisement and forbade it from using his name.
beats.reason: He distances himself from the promotion rather than testing any factual claim.

beats.text: The advertisement had received thousands of views before he responded.
beats.decisive_clue: refusal of association remains despite popularity
beats.reason: Audience size is not proof about the claim.

chains.feedback_short: Ben rejects his association with the advertisement; its popularity is beside the point.
chains.feedback_deep: Repudiate can mean disowning an association. Refute concerns disproving a proposition. A widely viewed advertisement can still be publicly disowned.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.attention: Look at what Ben is refusing to be part of.
hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Fatima’s response to the survey claim?

beats.text: Fatima produced the original responses: the article said eight people objected, but all eight had marked “agree.”
beats.decisive_clue: primary responses contradict the published assertion
beats.reason: She supplies verifiable evidence of an error.

beats.text: She showed the original forms to the editor rather than asking readers simply to trust her.
beats.decisive_clue: the underlying records remain available for checking
beats.reason: Access to the source reinforces the evidence-based demonstration.

chains.feedback_short: The original forms show the reported result was wrong, not merely unpopular.
chains.feedback_deep: Refutation involves giving reasons or evidence that establish an error. Fatima’s original forms directly undercut the article’s numerical claim.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.attention: Check whether her reply contains verifiable material.
hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

chains.frame: Which verb best describes Pavel’s response to the proposal?

beats.text: Pavel said, “I will not support excluding Maya from the trip, and I want no part of that plan.”
beats.decisive_clue: firmly rejected a proposed course of action
beats.reason: He refuses to accept or endorse the exclusion.

beats.text: He made the declaration after hearing everyone’s opinions.
beats.decisive_clue: firm rejection remains even after discussion
beats.reason: Listening beforehand does not amount to proving a claim false.

chains.feedback_short: Pavel refuses to endorse the plan; listening to others does not constitute disproof.
chains.feedback_deep: Repudiate applies naturally to refusing an idea or association. Refute requires a claim capable of being proved false and an argument or evidence against it.
chains.contrast_rule: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.

hints.attention: Does his response reject a proposal or prove a statement wrong?
hints.axis: To repudiate is to reject something firmly; to refute is to establish that it is false with proof or reasoning.
hints.contrast: Repudiate says no; refute shows why no.
